title: Work, energy and power
summary: Work as energy transfer, kinetic, gravitational and elastic potential energy, conservation of energy, power and efficiency, and the energy density of fuels.

keyterms.definition: Energy transferred when a force moves its point of application: W = Fs cos θ, in joules.
Energy of a moving mass: E_k = ½mv² = p²/2m.
Energy stored due to position in a gravitational field; near Earth, ΔE_p = mgΔh.
Energy stored in a stretched or compressed spring: E_H = ½kΔx².
Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred or transformed; the total in an isolated system is constant.
Rate of doing work or transferring energy, P = ΔW/Δt; for a constant force, P = Fv. Unit: watt.
Useful energy (or power) output divided by total energy (or power) input; always less than 1 in real devices.
Energy released per unit volume of a fuel, in J m⁻³.
Energy released per unit mass of a fuel, in J kg⁻¹.
A flow diagram whose arrow widths are proportional to energy, showing useful output and dissipated energy.

questions.prompt: A 40 N force pulls a sledge 5.0 m along level ground; the rope is at 60° to the horizontal. How much work does the force do?

questions.statement: A person holding a heavy box stationary does no mechanical work on it.
questions.explanation: The box does not move, so the displacement is zero and W = Fs cos θ = 0, even though muscles use chemical energy.

questions.text: A 1200 kg car travels at 20 m s⁻¹. Its kinetic energy is ___ kJ.

questions.prompt: If the speed of a car doubles, its kinetic energy
questions.explanation: E_k ∝ v², so doubling v quadruples E_k, which is why braking distances rise sharply with speed.

questions.text: A spring of stiffness 200 N m⁻¹ is stretched by 0.10 m. The elastic potential energy stored is ___ J.

questions.prompt: A 2.0 kg book is lifted from the floor onto a shelf 1.5 m high (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Its gain in GPE is
Match each expression to the energy it gives.
questions.explanation: Each expression gives a quantity measured in joules.

questions.statement: The area under a force–extension graph equals the work done stretching the object.
questions.explanation: Work = force × displacement summed over the extension, which is the area under the graph; for a spring this is ½kx².

questions.prompt: A ball of mass m has momentum p. Its kinetic energy is
questions.explanation: E_k = ½mv² and p = mv, so E_k = p²/2m.

questions.prompt: Friction does work on a sliding block. What happens to this energy?
options: It becomes internal (thermal) energy of the block and surface
It is stored as elastic energy
questions.explanation: Energy is conserved: work against friction is dissipated as internal energy, raising the temperature.

lessons.title: Conservation of energy, power and efficiency

questions.prompt: A stone falls from rest through 5.0 m (g = 9.8 m s⁻², no air resistance). What is its speed at the bottom?
questions.explanation: mgh = ½mv², so v = √(2gh) = √98 ≈ 9.9 m s⁻¹. Mass cancels.

questions.text: A motor lifts a 50 kg load through 4.0 m in 8.0 s (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). The useful power output is ___ W.

questions.statement: A car moving at constant velocity on a level road needs no engine power.
questions.explanation: Drag and rolling resistance oppose motion; the engine must supply P = Fv to balance them.

questions.prompt: A car’s engine supplies a driving force of 600 N at a steady 25 m s⁻¹. What is the useful power?

questions.text: A lamp takes in 60 J of electrical energy and gives out 9 J as light. Its efficiency is ___%.
questions.explanation: Efficiency = useful output / input = 9/60 = 0.15 = 15 %.

questions.prompt: In a Sankey diagram, the width of each arrow is proportional to
questions.explanation: Widths show amounts of energy, making losses easy to see; input width equals the total output width.

questions.prompt: Match each quantity to its SI unit.
questions.explanation: Energy density is per volume; specific energy is per mass.

questions.statement: Efficiency can be calculated using either energies or powers.
questions.explanation: Since power = energy/time over the same time interval, the ratio is the same.

questions.prompt: A 40 kg child slides down a slide 3.0 m high, reaching the bottom at 6.0 m s⁻¹ (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). About how much energy was dissipated?
questions.explanation: GPE lost = 40 × 9.8 × 3.0 = 1176 J; KE gained = ½ × 40 × 36 = 720 J; dissipated = 456 J.

questions.prompt: Order the energy transfers in a hydroelectric power station.
items: Kinetic energy of the rotating turbine
questions.explanation: At each stage some energy is dissipated, so overall efficiency is below 100 %.
